basics.name: Silvia Téliz
basics.label: PhD Candidate at the Annenberg School for Communication, University of Pennsylvania
basics.summary: I am a PhD candidate at the Annenberg School for Communication, University of Pennsylvania. My research explores the visual representation of social identity in Latin American political communication using computational methods.

work.name: Politics, Identities, and Communication Lab - Annenberg School for Communication, University of Pennsylvania
highlights: Contributed to collaborative research projects through computational data analysis, including the collection, cleaning, and processing of large datasets.
Provided intellectual input and drafted significant portions of resulting peer-reviewed manuscripts.

work.name: Center for Advanced Research in Global Communication - Annenberg School for Communication, University of Pennsylvania
work.summary: Worked under Dr. Juan Llamas Rodriguez's supervision on the development of a mixed-methods study on the representation of gender and skin color stereotypes in Mexican telenovelas and TV series (a report commissioned by the Luminate foundation).
highlights: Co-wrote a book chapter on colorism and cultural activism in Mexico for Planet Digital (NYU Press).

work.name: Children and Media - Annenberg School for Communication, University of Pennsylvania
highlights: Provided individual assistance and clarification during dedicated office hours.
Assisted the instructor with logistical tasks, such as managing the online learning platform and maintaining grade and attendance records.
Graded and provided dedicated feedback for assignments and final papers.
Assisted in designing and grading exams.
Taught lecture on racial representations in children's media.

work.name: Quantitative Methods for Communication Research - Universidad Panamericana, Mexico City
work.summary: Served as the Instructor of Record for an undergraduate-level course, delivering all lectures and directing all class activities for the Communication major.
highlights: Designed all educational materials, including original slides, assignments, tests, and lab activities.
Introduced the programming language R into the curriculum as the main tool for learning Quantitative Methods.
Held regular office hours for student assistance and managed the grading of all assignments, including weekly lab activities and final projects.
